name: Libya: western militia clashes and east-west rivalry
started: 2025-05-12 (approximate; Tripoli clashes after the killing of SSA leader al-Kikli, followed by Zawiya fighting in 2026)
summary: Libya remains split between the Tripoli-based government and the Haftar family's Libyan National Army. Violence in 2026 has been mostly militia fighting in the west, including a May battle at Zawiya that shut the country's largest working refinery, alongside targeted killings in the east.

sides.name: Western armed groups (nominally under the Tripoli-based GNU)
members: Counter Security Threats Agency and First Support Force (Muhammed Bahroun, 'al-Far')
Shuhada al-Nasr Brigade and Zawiya Petroleum Facilities Guard (Muhammad Kashlaf, 'al-Qasseb')
Salem al-Latif group and al-Kabwat (103rd Infantry Battalion)

sides.name: Libyan National Army (east and south)
backers: Russia (Africa Corps presence and high-level ties; Putin met Saddam Haftar on 21 Aug 2026)
leaders: Saddam Haftar (LNA chief of staff and apparent heir)

background: Since the 2020 ceasefire Libya has had rival governments in Tripoli and the east. In the west, armed groups funded by the state compete for territory, smuggling routes and access to oil infrastructure; in the east, Khalifa Haftar's LNA controls Cyrenaica and much of the south and has grown close to Russia.
This matters for the wider region because southeastern Libya is a reported supply route for Sudan's RSF, and because Russia's position in Libya supports its operations across the Sahel.
year: Saif al-Islam Gaddafi was shot dead in Zintan on 3 February 2026. In late February dozens of soldiers were killed on the Niger and Chad borders in an LNA-affiliated operation. On 5 to 10 May rival Zawiya militias fought around the refinery: the security directorate announced a campaign against criminal groups, mortars and artillery hit the refinery and nearby homes, and one side used improvised one-way attack drones on a scale not seen before in Libyan urban fighting. The refinery shut for two days. On 10 and 11 August drones struck the refinery three times in two days, and on 12 August an attack on a substation knocked out over 700 MW. The same day as the first drone attack, the LNA's intelligence chief Fawzi al-Mansouri was killed by a car bomb in Benghazi. On 21 August Putin met Saddam Haftar, and on 25 August the rival governments reached an initial agreement on overhauling the electoral system.
situation: As of October 2026 western Libya remains a patchwork of militias, with Zawiya the most volatile flashpoint near Tripoli. US-led unification talks have reportedly considered elevating Saddam Haftar, which the International Crisis Group warned could provoke resistance in the west.
technical: Zawiya, May 2026: mortars, artillery and improvised one-way attack drones; aviation kerosene tank No. 501 hit twice and No. 502 by gunfire; GECOL power plant damaged.
Casualties at Zawiya in May: 3 civilians killed and 9 injured (NIHRL); at least 10 militia fighters killed and 20 injured (local sources).
Al-Qasseb has been under UN, US, EU and UK sanctions since 2018; his tribe, the Awlad Abu Hmeira, has controlled the refinery since 2011.
August 2026: three drone attacks on the Zawiya refinery in two days and a substation attack that took over 700 MW of 1,300 MW offline.
The Haftars brokered releases of a US missionary held by IS Sahel and of two Russian Africa Corps soldiers held by Mali's FLA in August 2026, reportedly including ransom.

Russian footprint: the Africa Corps replaced Wagner in Libya from spring 2024, with estimates of 800 to 1,800 personnel (Wikipedia); daily Russian military flights from Hmeimim in Syria to three Libyan bases began in mid-December 2024 after Assad's fall (CEPA); a University of Texas and NGA Tearline study (June 2026) found improvements at six Libyan air bases since April 2024 that support operations into the Sahel.
Moscow wants a naval base at Tobruk; Haftar had not approved one as of early 2025 (CEPA).
casualties: Low by regional standards; no national total found. Zawiya in May 2026 killed at least 3 civilians and 10 fighters.
displaced: No significant new displacement figure found.

timeline.event: Saif al-Islam Gaddafi shot dead in Zintan.
Zawiya security campaign; shelling shuts the refinery.
LNA intelligence chief Fawzi al-Mansouri killed by a car bomb in Benghazi; first of three drone attacks on the Zawiya refinery.
Putin meets Saddam Haftar in Moscow.
Rival governments reach an initial agreement on electoral reform.

outlook: Watch Zawiya and Tripoli militia rivalries, any deal that elevates Saddam Haftar, and Russia's response to US-led unification efforts.

battles.name: Drone attacks on the Zawiya refinery
sides: Zawia Oil Refining Company and GECOL facilities
battles.outcome: Three drone attacks on the refinery in two days and an attack on a substation south of Zawiya.
battles.forces: Drones; perpetrators not identified in sources reviewed.
battles.losses: No casualty figures; over 700 MW of a 1,300 MW plant taken offline.
battles.significance: Shows Zawiya's militia rivalry has moved to stand-off drone attacks on national energy infrastructure.

battles.name: Battle of the Zawiya refinery
sides: Muhammed Bahroun ('al-Far') and the 'joint security forces'
Muhammad Kashlaf ('al-Qasseb'), Shuhada al-Nasr Brigade and Zawiya PFG, with al-Latif and al-Kabwat
battles.outcome: Council of Elders brokered a ceasefire on the evening of 8 May; 52nd Infantry Brigade separated the sides; refinery restarted by 10 May.
battles.forces: Mortars, artillery and improvised one-way attack drones.
battles.losses: 3 civilians killed and 9 injured (NIHRL); at least 10 fighters killed and 20 injured (local sources).
battles.significance: Shut Libya's largest working refinery and introduced large-scale drone use to Libyan urban militia fighting.
